text.p: Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South African mining firm Anglo-American Corp have announced they have formed a consortium to participate in the privatization auction of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD.
The government is selling off a 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD at an auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange April 29 for a minimum price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion).
Votorantim and Anglo-American will hold equal shares in the consortium named Valecom, the same name given to the 40-45 percent block which is being auctioned, the companies said.
Votorantim President Antonio Ermirio de Moraes will be made the head of the administration council of Valecom should the consortium emerge as the winning bidder from the auction.

The consortium will be drawing up a global action program for CVRD and its subsidiaries with the objective to preserve the entirety of the company's business and prevent the dismemberment of its different operations, the statement said.
Votorantim and Anglo-American will continue their negotiations with other companies, Brazilian pension funds and the employees of CVRD to recruit more members into the consortium, the statement said.

Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN is also forming a consortium and is looking to close a deal with pulp and paper firm Cia. Suzano, metal and metallurgical company Caemi, Nations Bank, Opportunity Asset Management, South Africa's Gencor and Brazilian pension funds.
A group of seven pension funds which jointly holds a 15 percent voting stake in CVRD still has to decide if and which consortium it will join to take part in the CVRD auction.
They are coveted by both consortia because whichever group wins the auction will have a controling position in CVRD if the pension funds are on its side.

A spokeswoman for the pension fund of Brazil's Central Bank, Centrus, said the fund would also be joining the Valecom consortium. Centrus, which does not belong to the group of seven funds, already holds a two percent voting stake in CVRD.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
